title: Tag Registry
content_html:
Tag Registry

Capability

/studio/tag-registry/ maintains canonical tags: browse/filter, create, edit, delete, and demote a tag into an alias. The table presents each tag's ordered document associations as current title links.

Canonical identity has wider consequences than visible registry rows. Delete/demotion can affect aliases and assignments, so server planners own impact calculation and cross-file mutation. Document associations are one-way references and never make Tag Registry the owner of document lifecycle.

Workflow

load registry + aliases + assignments
  -> filter/search or open mutation modal
  -> validate candidate ID/group/complete doc_url draft
  -> preview destructive or cross-file impact
  -> confirm
  -> server planner + atomic apply
  -> project the response + record activity evidence

Manual patch guidance exists only for explicitly supported fallback paths such as create and demote. Edit Tag document associations and destructive writes require the Local Studio tag service.

New Tag

New Tag submits {tag_id, group}. The server validates only the new candidate and configured Analysis tags destination, allocates a fresh immutable document ID, creates the source document, appends the registry row with its canonical Analysis URL at doc_url[0], rebuilds that exact child projection, and records create-tag activity as one transaction.

Creation does not audit or repair unrelated registry associations. The exclusive-create document write is the collision boundary and refuses to overwrite an existing destination.

Edit Tag

Edit keeps tag_id readonly while allowing the scalar group and complete ordered doc_url[] draft to change together. A group change validates affected alias constraints before the registry write.

The document editor:

  • renders current document titles as linked pills in stored URL order;
  • uses each pill's × to remove that exact association from the draft;
  • keeps an Analysis-only title picker visible with a fixed four-row scrolling result area;
  • fills the search field from one exact provider result and enables the adjacent + to append it; and
  • saves the complete array atomically or discards all draft changes on Close.

The picker exposes no free-form URL or ID entry and excludes exact URLs already in the draft. Equal visible titles are allowed because exact canonical URLs remain the association identity. Tag Registry intentionally suppresses report context in this compact picker; the committed provider record still retains it.

A title pill and the table link resolve against Studio's configured public preview base. An unresolved stored URL is shown as Unavailable document, remains linked to its exact location, and can be removed. A successful edit closes without echoing the verbose backend audit summary into the page; errors and warnings remain visible.

The route displays tag_id directly; canonical rows do not have a separate label. The Edit Tag modal uses the tag ID as its heading and exposes the four group pills as a single-choice control. It has no disabled identity field or duplicate current-group badge.

Durable Rules

  • canonical IDs are globally unique slug-safe names;
  • registry rows use tag_registry_v5 and contain exactly tag_id, group, doc_url, and updated_at_utc; they contain no tag-row label or description;
  • doc_url is an ordered array of zero or more supported canonical repository-relative Docs Viewer URLs;
  • exact URLs may be shared by several tags but cannot repeat within one row;
  • URL order is preserved but does not imply document ownership, uniqueness, or synchronization;
  • every tag has exactly one allowed scalar group, which is not part of the ID;
  • stale URLs remain valid stored associations and are not inferred, repaired, or replaced from titles or current context;
  • ordinary creation has its own focused planner/API and does not use registry import semantics or certify unrelated associations;
  • deletion and demotion must account for alias/assignment references;
  • deletion never deletes a linked document;
  • demotion replaces a canonical tag with an alias targeting selected remaining canonical tags; and
  • local-server mutations record one initiating action context in Admin activity.

Exact limits, request shapes, and effect payloads live in tag_source_model.py, focused planners, and tests.

Code Map

  • template/controller: tag-registry.html, tag-registry.js
  • state/render/modal/save modules: studio/app/frontend/js/tag-registry-*
  • HTTP boundary: studio/app/server/studio/studio_tag_api/registry.py, studio_tag_api/promotions.py
  • planners: studio/services/tags/tag_registry_mutations.py, tag_promotion_mutations.py
  • canonical source: studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json

The route root follows the shared Studio ready/busy contract. Mutation modal state is route mode; service availability reflects direct-write capability.

Weak Spots And Change Method

  • Provider titles depend on published document-location projections; a newly created or moved document is unavailable to the picker until the owning public projection is published.
  • Stale association inspection is present, but there is no automatic repair or bulk link workflow.
  • The compact Analysis-only picker can show equal titles without report disambiguation. That is accepted while collisions remain rare.
  • There is no UI for reordering URLs or adding Library/Studio URLs, even though the canonical schema supports their configured canonical routes.
  • Manual patch fallback cannot safely reproduce every cross-file mutation; keep its supported surface explicit.
  • The controller remains a large coordinator even after state/render/workflow modules were split.
  • Visible copy is code-owned in tag-ui-text.js, so it can drift from server terminology.

Change the domain planner and tests before the modal/controller. Add UI detail here only when it reveals a durable workflow or ownership boundary.
